title: Version-level acceptance on fresh batches: one merged candidate per step, judged by a paired item-bootstrap lower bound on training items that were never used to write rules
verdict_cn: 结论：可行，建议下一版采用，但不会凭空造出效果。做法：每步把留下的规则合成一份新版Skill（附在解题模型提示后的说明），整份收或不收；用一批没用来写过规则的训练题判断，新旧两版同轮各答一遍、逐题比对错，按题重抽样估出“有95%把握的最低提升”，它大于0且平均提升至少2分（百分制）才收。用过的题放回题库，不设固定验证集，但和上一版v3（逐条规则先筛选再复核）一样要用带答案的训练题。实测：同一文本重跑，每题差值的波动（标准差）跑2次0.22、4次0.14；真实的+9分效果是0.34和0.31，所以要加题而非多跑。要有八成把握认出+5、+3、+2分，跑2次分别约需213–274、487–733、1016–1637道题。SearchQA（问答，600道）和LiveMath（数学，283道）能认出约4–6分；OfficeQA（办公文档问答）、表格题和ALFWorld（文字家务游戏）题太少，只能认出约10–15分以上。成本：五阶段合计，从空白说明起步约1350万token（模型计费单位），v3实耗1400万；从任务说明起步约3900万，v3为6000万。试点：130道新题、1560次作答、约240万token：任务说明版高16分被收，重复文本和两句无关文字被拒。风险：空白起点上一句无关的话也曾被收下（+3.6分）；从任务说明起步时v3的7条规则都无可测提升，新方法可能什么都收不下。
what_i_did:
Read context.md in full. All extraction was read-only.

1. Cal-1 main round, old machine: 11 arms x 200 SearchQA training items x 4 runs = 8,800 verdict cells. The per-arm totals, the registered noise floor (+0.0075, sd 0.1438, 22/18/160) and the positive effect (+0.0938, 48/13/139) all reproduce exactly.
2. The D1 v2 fresh-batch pilot, new machine: 1,560 cells.
3. The v3 run's train/screen/confirm cells for both chains: 14,178 records. A script asserted that no evaluation/test/holdout/final/reserve path was touched; selftest cells were not opened. I also read the halves in prepare/unit.json and the ledger settle events.

Analyses:
- Per-item paired-difference SD at k = 1, 2, 4 runs (averaged over all run-subset pairs, item-bootstrap 95% CIs), and the between-item spread tau from Var(d) = tau^2 + W/k.
- Power: analytic bounds, plus a fully empirical simulation that resamples cal-1 items and runs. Two effect-mixture models; k = 1/2/4; delta = 0/0.02/0.03/0.05/0.09; n = 50-4,000; 2,000 batches x 1,000 exact-multinomial percentile-bootstrap resamples. Also type-I error and the winner's curse.
- Replays of the D1 decision on cal-1, on the pilot, and rule by rule on v3's screen/confirm data, using each rule's never-shown check half.
- A subgroup split of v3's only screen-passer, a day-to-day drift check, a futility-stopping simulation, and a per-step cost comparison against v3 receipts.
- Checked GEPA's acceptance rule in the arXiv HTML and checked the adaptive-data-analysis references (reusable holdout, Ladder).

Wrote the report. The fresh-batch pilot (2.39M tokens) was launched by the previous D1 round on the new machine and is analysed for the first time here. No new paid call was made in this round.
evidence:
[M] cal-1, 200 items:
- Same text re-run (parent:B - parent:A): paired SD 0.326 / 0.222 [0.191, 0.251] / 0.144 [0.114, 0.173] at k = 1/2/4; tau = 0.
- Real +0.094 effect (ids-full, 48 up / 13 down / 139 tie): SD 0.402 / 0.344 [0.297, 0.388] / 0.310 [0.263, 0.355]; tau 0.273 [0.217, 0.320].
- Every text change, placebos included, has tau 0.12-0.28. More items, not more runs, buy power.

[M] Pilot, 130 fresh SearchQA training items x 2 runs, 6 arms (0 unknown, 0 truncated):
- Task card vs empty scaffold: +0.162 [+0.104, +0.223], 28 up / 2 down.
- Same good text twice: +0.004, SD2 0.159.
- Two placebos on the good text: 0.000 and -0.023 (tau 0.06-0.14).
- Recipe placebo on the scaffold: -0.081 [-0.142, -0.023], replicating cal-1's -0.098.

[E] Items needed for 80% power (one-sided 95% item-bootstrap LB > 0; mix / mixchurn models):

| delta | k = 2 | k = 4 | k = 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.05 | 213 / 274 | 156 / 209 | 346 / 406 |
| 0.03 | 487 / 733 | 315 / 535 | 881 / 1,116 |
| 0.02 | 1,016 / 1,637 | 593 / 1,127 | 1,895 / 2,327 |

- Analytic n80 at k = 2: 762/339/122 using the same-text SD, 1,826/811/292 using the seeds' SD.
- Type I error 0.035-0.057.
- One run on more items is cheapest per call: 500 x 1 matches 300 x 2 with 17% fewer cells.
- Winner's curse: the accepted estimate is inflated 1.34-1.51x at delta 0.03, n 300, k 2.

[E] Smallest effect each pool can certify at 80% power (tau 0.2): SearchQA 0.042 (300 x 2), LiveMath 0.056 (233 x 2), OfficeQA 0.103 (37 x 4), SpreadsheetBench 0.122 (46 x 2), ALFWorld 0.153 (29 x 2).

[M] Replays:
- cal-1: accepts ids-full and seed-only (LB +0.058); rejects parent:B, seed-rule, seed-rule3, cand and controls 1/3/4. It also accepts the control:2 placebo (+0.036, LB +0.011).
- Pilot: accepts S; rejects the duplicate and all placebos.
- v3 data: E-ds s1-r2 (an answer-format rule) scored +0.081 on its 99-item never-shown check half (p1 = 0.0034; the Bonferroni threshold over 17 arms is 0.0029). v3 had rejected it on a 1/4-item C1 gain from 6 trigger items, while its C2 rest was +41/4.
- All 7 I-ds rule arms: -0.107 to +0.005 on their check halves.
- v3's only screen-passer, s1-r1: +0.266 on its 8 evidence items but -0.047 [-0.094, -0.003] on the other 186.

[M] Drift: the same scaffold on the same items passed 0.743 on 10/19 and 0.683 on 10/20 (-0.060 [-0.098, -0.021]). Seeds minus scaffold was +0.033 on 10/19 and +0.090 on 10/20.

[M/E] Cost over five stages:
- v3 gate, measured: E 13.97M / I 60.22M.
- D1, two-arm rounds only: E 12.00M / I 34.13M.
- D1 with a parent duplicate and one placebo arm in the chain's first round: 13.50M / 38.85M.
- D1 with both in every stage's first round: 19.85M / 58.75M.
- The futility look saves 27-46% of a round on null or harmful packages and costs at most 0.01 power.
design:
Step t on bench b runs in seven parts.

1. **Proposal batch B_p.** Size n_p = v3's proposal half: SearchQA 100, LiveMath 50, OfficeQA 37, SpreadsheetBench 45, ALFWorld 28. It is drawn from unflagged pool items, or from flagged ones once only n_a unflagged remain. B_p is flagged permanently and becomes learning material only.
2. **Learn as in v4, on B_p only.** Parent rollout, examiner, analyst, preparation, and selftest on evidence items inside B_p. If no rule survives, there is no round and S_{t+1} = S_t.
3. **Freeze one candidate.** Parent plus every surviving rule, merged exactly as it would be deployed (one text, one hash). No per-rule arms, no composite round, no pruning after the round.
4. **Acceptance batch B_a.** Drawn from never-proposed-on items, least-used first, seeded. Sizes: SearchQA 300 x 2 (or 500 x 1), LiveMath 233 x 2 (183 x 2 if two steps), OfficeQA 37 x 4, SpreadsheetBench 46 x 2, ALFWorld 29 x 2. If fewer than n_min items are available, the step is recorded as "underpowered" with its power and makes no decision.
5. **One interleaved round.**
   - Parent and candidate on B_a x k.
   - In the chain's first round only, also a parent duplicate and a length-matched placebo arm. Later rounds estimate re-run noise from each arm's own k >= 2 runs.
   - Regression panels: 60 items per earlier bench (parent 2 runs, candidate 1).
   - Parent cells are never reused from another round.
6. **Decision.**
   - d_i = per-item mean(candidate) - mean(parent).
   - Accept iff the one-sided 95% percentile item-bootstrap LB(mean d) > 0 and mean d >= 0.02.
   - Earlier benches must pass non-inferiority (margins from D8), with at most 2 extra format violations.
   - Optional futility look at n_a/2: reject if mean d <= 0.
7. **Return to the pool.**
   - B_a stays unflagged (usage +1). It can serve later decisions and can later become proposal material, at which point it is flagged.
   - No model role ever sees B_a outcomes; at most the accept/reject bit (the Ladder bound).
   - At most 3 steps per stage reuse one batch.

**Attribution** happens only after acceptance and is descriptive:
- applicability subgroups, with items marked from their texts only;
- leave-one-out arms on the next step's fresh batch, for packages of at most 3 rules;
- removing a rule creates a new candidate, judged on a later batch.

**Why this is not a fixed validation set:**
- No item is reserved from learning for the run; an item is set aside for one decision at most.
- Selection items are redrawn every step from the same training pool the method learns from, and go back afterwards.
- Test sets and benches not yet reached are never touched.
- This is the registered category: registration 10/16 section 2.2 says "no separate held-out validation partition", and the owner decided on 10/16 that the gate uses real training items.
- What it does not avoid: like v3, it uses labelled training items to decide. If that reading is disallowed, only generated items (D6) remain.

**What the paper's claim becomes:** "Every accepted version improved accuracy on fresh training items it was not built from, with at most 5% false acceptance per decision, non-inferiority on earlier benchmarks, and batch sizes set by a pre-registered power analysis."
- Per-rule effects are descriptive only.
- Effect sizes come from the test evaluations, not the acceptance estimate.
- Null outcomes are reported with their power, e.g. 84-89% for +0.05 at 300 x 2 on SearchQA.
- Content claims need a placebo reference (a placebo chain for the paper).

risks:
1. **Small pools.** OfficeQA (74), SpreadsheetBench (91) and ALFWorld (57) can only certify effects of about 0.10-0.15. Only their first step gets fresh proposal material, and later steps reuse the same acceptance batch.
2. **There may be no effect to find.** On the good-instruction chain, no measured v3 rule shows a version-level effect (7 arms, -0.107 to +0.005), and cal-1's rule-shaped texts are <= 0. A D1 chain may accept nothing. D1 fixes the measuring instrument, not the proposals.
3. **Placebo acceptance on a weak parent.** An irrelevant sentence scored +0.036 with LB +0.011 on the empty scaffold, so content claims need a placebo reference.
4. **Heterogeneity can hide harm.** v3's screen-passer scored +0.266 on its own 8 evidence items and -0.047 on the other 186 items. Report up/down counts and subgroups.
5. **Day-to-day drift.** The same comparison measured +0.033 on one day and +0.090 the next. Both arms must be measured in the same round, and test-day conditions can differ from acceptance-day conditions.
6. **Winner's curse.** Acceptance estimates are inflated 1.3-2x at low power and must never be reported as effect sizes.
7. **Weak regression checks.** At 60 items, non-inferiority resolves only about 0.07-0.11.
8. **Power-model assumptions.** Heterogeneity was measured only on SearchQA, and the real-effect heterogeneity only on the empty scaffold; the other benches use an assumed tau. The simulation draws from a population of 200 items.
9. **Cost of controls.** With a duplicate and a placebo arm in every stage, D1 costs more than v3 on the empty-scaffold chain (19.9M vs 14.0M).
10. **Throughput.** About 880 cells/h at 6 workers. One ALFWorld round on the seeded chain costs about 16.4M tokens.
11. **Label use.** If the owner reads "no fixed validation set" as "no labelled real item may decide acceptance", neither v3 nor D1 qualifies.

**Per acceptance round** (receipt tokens, priced at v3's measured per-cell receipts; D1 is estimated, v3 is measured):

|---|---|---|
| SearchQA, 300 x 2 | 1.50M (E) / 4.72M (I) | 4.54M / 7.42M |
| ALFWorld, I chain | 16.41M | 38.85M |

**Five stages, one round per step:**

| configuration | E chain | I chain |
|---|---|---|
| v3, measured | 13.97M | 60.22M |
| D1, two-arm rounds | 12.00M | 34.13M |
| D1 + parent duplicate and one placebo arm in the chain's first round | 13.50M | 38.85M |
| D1 + both in every stage's first round | 19.85M | 58.75M |

- The D1 totals assume a round at every step, including the two steps where v3 spent nothing.
- Leave-one-out attribution (3 rules) adds about 3x one duplicate arm, i.e. 3 x 0.75M = 2.25M (E) or 3 x 2.36M = 7.09M (I) at SearchQA s1.
- The futility look saves 27-46% of a round on null or harmful packages.
- D1's training rollout covers only B_p, about half of v3's 4.87M (E) / 16.0M (I).
- Wall-clock: about 1.4 h for a 1,200-cell SearchQA round.

**Spent in this direction:** pilot 2,388,219 tokens; earlier stopped attempt 112,525; v2 smoke 18,549. Total about 2.52M. This round spent 0.

**Next suggested pilot:** the merged I-ds s1 package vs the five-seed Skill, 2 arms x 130 fresh items x 2 runs, about 2.1M tokens.
recommendation:
Adopt D1 as the v5 acceptance rule. Its parts:
- One merged candidate per step.
- Acceptance on a fresh, never-proposed-on batch in one interleaved round, with LB95 > 0 and mean gain >= 0.02.
- Non-inferiority on earlier benches, using D8's margins.
- A parent duplicate and one length-matched placebo arm in the chain's first round; in every stage only if the budget allows.
- A futility look at half the batch.
- Descriptive attribution only after acceptance.

Registered sizes:
- SearchQA: 300 x 2, or 500 x 1.
- LiveMath: 183-233 x 2.
- The three small pools: all unflagged items x 2-4 runs, with their delta80 printed in the registration.

Start from the task-card instruction (the owner's yardstick) and pre-register that the chain may accept nothing, with the power statement as the result. Pair D1 with D8 (regression margins and alpha across steps), with D6 (generated items for the small pools), and with a placebo chain for the content claim.

Next step before a full run: the roughly 2.1M-token pilot of a real learned package on the good-instruction parent, to measure tau in the realistic case.
